instruction: One-hot encode the values of the color column.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
enc = OneHotEncoder(sparse_output=False)
X = enc.fit_transform(df[['color']])

instruction: Encode categories as consecutive integers with an ordinal encoder.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import OrdinalEncoder
enc = OrdinalEncoder()
X = enc.fit_transform(df[['size']])

instruction: One-hot encode while mapping unknown categories at transform time to all zeros.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
enc = OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore', sparse_output=False)
X = enc.fit_transform(df[['city']])

instruction: Turn string class labels into integers 0 through n-1.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder
y = LabelEncoder().fit_transform(labels)

instruction: Binarize label vectors, collapsing all non-zero classes into a single 1 column.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelBinarizer
Y = LabelBinarizer().fit_transform(y)

instruction: Encode a multi-label target where each sample carries several tags at once.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import MultiLabelBinarizer
mlb = MultiLabelBinarizer()
Y = mlb.fit_transform(tag_lists)

instruction: Drop one dummy column after one-hot encoding to avoid perfect multicollinearity.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
enc = OneHotEncoder(drop='first', sparse_output=False)
X = enc.fit_transform(df[['color']])

instruction: Print the column names produced by a fitted OneHotEncoder.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
enc = OneHotEncoder(sparse_output=False).fit(df[['city']])
print(enc.get_feature_names_out())

instruction: Encode rare and previously unseen categories as the integer -1.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import OrdinalEncoder
enc = OrdinalEncoder(handle_unknown='use_encoded_value', unknown_value=-1)
X = enc.fit_transform(df[['sku']])

instruction: Fit a categorical encoder on training data only and reuse it on the test set.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
enc = OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore', sparse_output=False)
Xtr = enc.fit_transform(train_df[['city']])
Xte = enc.transform(test_df[['city']])

instruction: Quickly one-hot encode a DataFrame column with pandas get_dummies.
output:
import pandas as pd
X = pd.get_dummies(df, columns=['city'], dtype=int)

instruction: Target-encode a high-cardinality feature using only training labels.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import TargetEncoder
enc = TargetEncoder()
Xtr = enc.fit_transform(train_df[['sku']], y_train)
Xte = enc.transform(test_df[['sku']])

instruction: Map a yes/no column to the integers 1 and 0.
output: df['flag'] = df['flag'].map({'yes': 1, 'no': 0})

instruction: Supply an explicit list of allowed categories to the encoder.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import OrdinalEncoder
enc = OrdinalEncoder(categories=[['S', 'M', 'L', 'XL']])
X = enc.fit_transform(df[['size']])

instruction: Replace each category by the number of times it appears in the data.
output:
counts = df['city'].value_counts()
df['city_count'] = df['city'].map(counts)

instruction: Group infrequent categories into a single bucket during one-hot encoding.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
enc = OneHotEncoder(min_frequency=5, sparse_output=False)
X = enc.fit_transform(df[['city']])

instruction: Map the integers produced by a LabelEncoder back to the original strings.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder
le = LabelEncoder().fit(labels)
y = le.transform(labels)
print(le.inverse_transform(y))

instruction: Encode the days of the week in a custom order from Monday to Sunday.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import OrdinalEncoder
days = [['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed', 'Thu', 'Fri', 'Sat', 'Sun']]
enc = OrdinalEncoder(categories=days)
X = enc.fit_transform(df[['day']])

instruction: Print the shape of the encoded matrix so you can see how many dummies were created.
output:
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
X = OneHotEncoder(sparse_output=False).fit_transform(df[['city']])
print(X.shape)

instruction: Produce a dense one-hot array instead of a sparse matrix.
